mod.overview: Ultra Shifter Duel is the {TKO} clan's 'Ultra-Shifter_SG1_Duel' build (scripts.vol dated 2003-09-04, by {TKO}Arkangel according to its entry-script notes): Emo1313's 09-28-2000 Shifter nine-armor class system with every weapon pushed to an almost instant fire cycle, ammunition limits in the hundreds, a few new toys (a Guard Dog turret, a Plasma Stinger rocket, a multi-disc volley) and, on duel maps, the Dread Duel and Dread Tournament game scripts that turn the server into a one-on-one arena. Compared with the Shifter it descends from, it plays as a fast, high-ammo free-for-all rather than a slow class-based base game.
notes: Lineage: the item, armor and projectile scripts match Shifter 09-28-2000 (and its {TKO} SG1 edit) far more closely than GreyFlcn's v1G, which is why they keep weapon and pack code in item.cs rather than v1G's gundata.cs, packdata.cs and deploydata.cs. It does not have SG1's ArkAngel and DarthAngel armors, and none of v1G's tournament systems. The notes below compare against Shifter.

Fire rates: the ItemImageData of almost every weapon has reload and fire times cut to a few hundredths of a second (Chaingun 0.02, Plasma Gun 0.03, Mortar 0.05, Disc Launcher 0, Rocket Launcher 0, Boom Stick, Dart Rifle, Magnum and Rail Gun 0.03-0.13, Vulcan reload 0.01). The Shifter Plasma Gun and Mortar fire modes are not in the firing code any more (see those items), while the Rocket Launcher and Disc Launcher gained new modes.

Ammo scale: $ItemMax ammo limits are raised about tenfold (for example BulletAmmo 999, DiscAmmo 215, PlasmaAmmo 340, RocketAmmo 45-55 on armors that carry them), $SellAmmo and $AmmoPackMax values are higher, and the ammo stations (station_func.cs itemsToResupply) resupply hundreds of rounds at a time.

Armor changes (ArmorData.cs): weapon slots are raised (DreadNaught and Engineer 5, Heavy 6, Chemeleon 4), most armors have lower jet energy drain and stronger jump impulse or top speed, Heavy armor (used by the duel games) can carry the Sniper Rifle, Engineer Repair-Gun, Flight Pack and Guard Dog, Chemeleon the Sniper Rifle, and Mercenary the Mortar. Laser damage is split in damage.cs between $LaserDamageType and a second type, $Laser2DamageType, which no script ever defines; sniperLaser07 (the Laser Rifle's beam) and the turret ELF beam's $MiniELFDamageType are likewise undefined.

New items: the Guard Dog turret pack (ConPack), the Plasma Stinger rocket mode, the multi-disc volley, and the Super Sniper Rifle and Super Boom Stick (SuperSPRifle, SBoomStick), which are defined but granted only by commented-out 'PORT-OFF' remote commands in bindings.cs, so they are not obtainable in play. Deployed air bases and emplacements are bigger (see those items).

Station and server settings: the remote inventory list also allows the Airbase, Arbitor and EMP Beacon packs, Emplacement, Tactical Nuke (and its ammo) and Power Generator packs, and a Deployable Inventory pack in the vehicle list. serverConfig.cs turns on turret-kill credit ($Shifter::TurretKill) and sets 25 DetPacks and 12 nukes per match, laser-mine life 7, random missions off, power check off and the swearing filter off. The host-specific lines (name, port, passwords, telnet) are commented out with PORT-OFF markers. UltraShifterDuel.cs is the port's entry script, adding a few helper functions the scripts call but nothing defines, and does not change game behavior.

Dread Duel (duelmod.cs): an arena game switched on by a duel map's exec(duelmod). Players challenge each other (DuelPropose; the target has 30 seconds to accept, or can disable duels), are moved to one of 12 spawn spots (MissionGroup/Duel1-12) in Heavy armor, locked in observer view through a 7-second countdown, then fight to the first kill. Before spawning each player picks four weapons from a list of 14 (Rocket Launcher, Mortar, Plasma Gun, Shockwave Cannon, Disc Launcher, Grenade Launcher, Vulcan, Equalizer, ELF Gun, Rail Gun, Magnum, Boom Stick, Grav Gun, Sniper Rifle) and one pack (Rocket, Energy, Shield, Ammo, Repair or Flight). The winner scores a point and a win streak, the kill time is tracked against a best-time record, both players go back to observing, and a duel where both run out of ammo is a draw. Thrown mines are replaced by one tracked anti-personnel mine type that is cleared when the duel ends. Script bug: the pack table sets $DuelRealPack[5] twice (RepairPack then FlightPack) and never sets slot 6, so picking 'Repair Pack' gives a Flight Pack and picking 'Flight Pack' gives no pack. It also expects a DuelRecord.cs file that is not shipped.

Dread Tournament (duelmatch.cs): a knockout version for a duel map. Players ready up (Press FIRE when ready), then the game pairs them off at random (InitPartners and AssignPartner) and runs one duel at a time in DreadNaught armor with a choice of 10 weapons (the Blaster replaces the duel list's extras) and five packs. Each loser is eliminated, winners are paired again round by round ('about to duel for first place' for the last two), and the last survivor wins before the server moves to the next mission. The archive shipped no duel maps (the entry script says the host must add HaVoC / Meltdown style duel maps), so stock maps play as plain Shifter.

Chaingun.summary: Chaingun, still called the Equalizer in its on-use message and in the duel menus: a bullet weapon with explosive-tipped rounds that here has no spin-up delay and fires on a 0.02 second cycle.
notes: Unlike Shifter, ChaingunImage is weaponType 0 with 0.1 second spin-up and spin-down (Shifter: a spinning weapon with 0.2 second spin-up, 3 second spin-down and 0.2 second fire time), accuFire on, the muzzle light commented out, and the debris small-explosion sound as its fire sound; the spin sounds are commented out.

The ItemData description is 'Chaingun' (Shifter: 'Equalizer') and its hud icon is 'sniper' (Shifter: 'chain'). Chaingun::onUse still prints 'Using Equalizer', and duelmod.cs and duelmatch.cs list it as 'Equalizer'. ItemMsgs also defines Equalizer::onUse, but no Equalizer item exists.

ChaingunBullet is unchanged from Shifter: an explosive round with a small blast radius and its own Equalizer damage type. Equalizer damage is scaled by armor: Heavy 1.3x, Arbitor 1.2x, Goliath 1.1x, DreadNaught 0.8x, Engineer 0.7x.
Carried by DreadNaught, Engineer, Heavy, Assassin, Mercenary, Scout, Stim and Chemeleon; not by Goliath, Arbitor or Juggernaught. BulletAmmo limits are in the hundreds (999 on most armors).
Chaingun.source: item.cs ItemData Chaingun, ChaingunImage; baseProjData.cs ChaingunBullet; itemmsgs.cs Chaingun::onUse; ArmorData.cs; damage.cs

PlasmaGun.summary: Plasma Gun that fires a plain PlasmaBolt on a 0.03 second cycle. Shifter's Plasma fire modes are gone from the firing code, although the menu, key bindings and on-use message for them are still present.
notes: This mod has no PlasmaGunImage::onFire (Shifter has one that picks the projectile from the player's Plasma setting). PlasmaGunImage now just names ammoType PlasmaAmmo and projectileType PlasmaBolt, with reload and fire times of 0.03 seconds (Shifter 0.1 and 0.5), so no script code runs when it fires.

The Plasma Options menu and the remoteweapon_plasma_regular/_rapid/_multi bindings still set %client.Plasma to 0, 1 or 2, and PlasmaGun::onUse prints 'Standard', 'Rapid Fire' or 'Spread Fire', but nothing reads the setting when firing, so the choice only changes the message. The first test in PlasmaGun::onUse compares %client.rocket instead of %client.Plasma, so the 'Standard' line also appears whenever the Rocket Launcher setting is 0.
Hits on enemies by plasma damage ignite them about one time in five (Goliaths cannot be ignited). Arbitor takes 1.5x plasma damage, Goliath 0.5x.
Carried by Goliath, DreadNaught, Engineer, Heavy, Assassin, Mercenary, Scout/Stim and Chemeleon; not by Arbitor or Juggernaught.
PlasmaGun.source: item.cs PlasmaGunImage, ItemData PlasmaGun; itemmsgs.cs PlasmaGun::onUse; bindings.cs remoteweapon_plasma_*; baseProjData.cs PlasmaBolt; player.cs; ArmorData.cs

Mortar.summary: The Mortar, firing only the standard MortarShell on a 0.05 second cycle. Shifter's EMP, frag and MDM shell modes have been removed from the firing code.
notes: This mod has no MortarImage::onFire (Shifter has one that chooses between MortarShell, EMPMortar, BomberShell and a remotely detonated DelayMortarShell). MortarImage now names projectileType MortarShell with reload and fire times of 0.05 seconds (Shifter 0.5 and 1.0).

Mortar::onUse still prints 'Standard Shell', 'EMP Shell', 'Frag Shell' or 'MDM Shell' from %client.mortar, and the Weapon Options menu still lists Mortar Options for Heavy, DreadNaught, Juggernaught and Goliath, but bindings.cs defines no remoteweapon_mortar_* functions and nothing reads the setting when firing, so there is no way to change the shell. The first test in Mortar::onUse compares %client.rocket instead of %client.mortar.
Unlike Shifter, Mercenary armors can carry the Mortar (ArmorData.cs adds Mortar and MortarAmmo for marmor and mfemale), in addition to Goliath, DreadNaught, Heavy and Juggernaught.
The shell is a heavy splash shell: a large blast radius and mortar damage type.
Mortar.source: item.cs MortarImage, ItemData Mortar; itemmsgs.cs Mortar::onUse; admin.cs weaponoptions; bindings.cs; baseProjData.cs MortarShell; ArmorData.cs

DiscLauncher.summary: Disc Launcher with two firing modes: a standard disc, or a multi-disc volley of three slower discs for one disc of ammo.
notes: DiscLauncherImage::onFire is new (Shifter has none). Mode 0 (the default) spends 1 disc, plays the disc-fire sound and fires DiscShell. Mode 1 spends 1 disc and fires three DiscShell1 projectiles, each spawned with a different velocity argument (1 0 0, -1 0 0 and 0 0 0, rotated to the player's facing by EmplacementPack::rotVector), which spreads them out.
DiscShell1 is a slower, weaker disc than DiscShell (muzzle velocity 75 against 150, damage 0.5 against 0.6, same blast radius), so one volley can deal up to three hits of 0.5 for one disc of ammo.

The mode comes from the Disc Options menu entries 'Standard Fire' and 'Multi-Disc Fire' (remoteweapon_disc_regular and remoteweapon_disc_rapid set %client.disc to 0 or 1). DiscLauncher::onUse prints 'Using Disc Launcher - Standard' or '- Multi-Disc Fire'.
The image fires with fireTime 0 and reloadTime 0.05 (Shifter: weaponType 3, 1.25 second fire time, 0.25 second spin-up). With no disc ammo the new onFire does nothing and prints no message.
Carried by every armor except Arbitor and Juggernaught.
DiscLauncher.source: item.cs DiscLauncherImage::onFire, DiscLauncherImage; itemmsgs.cs DiscLauncher::onUse; bindings.cs remoteweapon_disc_*; baseProjData.cs DiscShell, DiscShell1; admin.cs weapon_disc; ArmorData.cs

EnergyRifle.summary: The ELF gun: a sustained lightning beam that drains the target's energy while hurting them.
notes: The only script difference from stock is the 'Using ELF Gun' bottom print; the beam does electricity damage and drains energy.
Electricity damage ignores the Shield Pack. Arbitor takes 0.2x, Mercenary 0.6x and Heavy 1.5x electricity damage.
Carried by DreadNaught, Engineer, Heavy, Assassin, Mercenary, Scout/Stim and Chemeleon.
EnergyRifle.source: item.cs ItemData EnergyRifle; itemmsgs.cs EnergyRifle::onUse; baseProjData.cs lightningCharge1, Lightning::damageTarget; player.cs; damage.cs

RocketLauncher.summary: Rocket Launcher with four modes: plain stinger, target-locking stinger, Plasma Stinger and wire guided. The LockJaw mode of Shifter has been replaced by the Plasma Stinger.
notes: Mode 0 fires a straight StingerMissile. Mode 1 (Locking Stinger) uses the line of sight: if the crosshair is on a player or flier within 500 m it fires a seeking StingerMissileTracker, tells the shooter 'Lock Aquired' and warns the target; otherwise it fires a plain stinger. The Locking entry in the Stinger Options menu is only offered while $Shifter::LockOn is true (it is in serverConfig.cs; an admin can turn it off). The Chemeleon exemption is written with '||' and is always true, so Chemeleons can be locked.

Mode 2, new here, fires PlasmaStingerMissile, an unguided missile with the Stinger's speed and blast radius but a larger damage value (0.65 against 0.5). It is chosen with remoteweapon_rocket3 ('Plasma Stinger Initiated'); the menu entry is labelled 'Plasma Rockets' and the on-use text 'Plasma Stinger Mode'. The Shifter LockJaw branch is gone from RocketImage::onFire.

Mode 3 (Wire Guided) fires a GodHammerMortar; half a second later and then every 0.25 seconds (up to 50 times, and only while it has moved more than 8 units) it is replaced by a GodHammer rocket spawned from the shooter's current muzzle aim, so the missile follows where you point.

Every mode spends 1 RocketAmmo; with none it says 'You have no Ammo for the Rocket Launcher'. The image fires with fireTime 0 and reloadTime 0.2 (Shifter 1.0 and 0.8). Using it prints the current mode.
Carried by Goliath, DreadNaught, Engineer, Juggernaught and Mercenary.
RocketLauncher.source: item.cs RocketImage::onFire, Tracker; itemmsgs.cs RocketLauncher::onUse; bindings.cs remoteweapon_rocket*; baseProjData.cs StingerMissile*, PlasmaStingerMissile, GodHammerMortar; admin.cs weapon_rocket

SuperSPRifleAmmo.summary: Sniper Bullet, the ammunition item for the Super Sniper Rifle. It adds nothing but a counter.
notes: $WeaponAmmo[SuperSPRifle] points at it. It appears in no $ItemMax list, no inventory list and no station resupply, so nothing in the scripts gives a normal player this ammo.
The only code that grants it is a commented-out remote command in bindings.cs marked PORT-OFF (setItemCount SuperSPRifle 1 and SuperSPRifleAmmo 2500).

SuperSPRifle.summary: Sniper Rifle (the Super Sniper Rifle): an extremely fast one-shot-class sniper projectile weapon that is defined but cannot be obtained through normal play.
notes: SuperSPRifleImage has reloadTime 0 and fireTime 0 and no onFire function, so the engine fires SuperSPRound whenever the trigger is held, using one SuperSPRifleAmmo each time; how fast that is in practice is not determined from the scripts.

SuperSPRound is a rocket-type projectile with impact damage of 0.99, the sniper damage type (the same type Shifter's head-shot and weapon-knock rules test for in player.cs), a muzzle velocity of 13500 and a very small blast radius.
Unlike the ordinary Sniper Rifle, it uses its own ammo and projectile, the sniper shape file and the targeting-laser hud icon.

It is in no armor's $ItemMax list, no $InvList or $RemoteInvList, and no spawn list; the only script that grants it is a commented-out PORT-OFF remote command in bindings.cs. The duel scripts do not list it either.
SuperSPRifle.source: item.cs SuperSPRifleImage, ItemData SuperSPRifle; baseProjData.cs SuperSPRound; bindings.cs

SBoomAmmo.summary: Boom Shell, the shotgun ammunition for the Super Boom Stick.
notes: $WeaponAmmo[SBoomStick] points at it, and SBoomStickImage::onFire spends one per shot.

Like the Super Sniper items it is in no $ItemMax list (only a stray $ItemMax[sarmor, BoomAmmo] = 61 line, which names the ordinary BoomAmmo) and no inventory list; the only script that grants it is a commented-out PORT-OFF remote command in bindings.cs (SBoomStick 1, SBoomAmmo 100).

SBoomStick.summary: Boom Stick (the Super Boom Stick): the shotgun with 19 pellets per shot, each pellet hitting several times harder than the ordinary Boom Stick's, defined but not obtainable through normal play.
notes: SBoomStickImage::onFire spends 1 SBoomAmmo and spawns 19 SBoomStickBlast bullets from the muzzle, the same pellet count as the ordinary BoomStick. With no shells it says 'Out Of Shells'.

SBoomStickBlast copies BoomStickBlast (impact bullet, boom stick damage type, muzzle velocity 200, one second flight) but with damage 0.38 per pellet instead of 0.08. Both shotguns here use a 0.08 second fire time and a 0.03 second reload.
It uses the shotgun shape and the blaster hud icon, priced like the ordinary Boom Stick, and the mortar fire and reload sounds.
It is in no armor's $ItemMax list, no $InvList or $RemoteInvList, and no spawn list; the only script that grants it is a commented-out PORT-OFF remote command in bindings.cs.
SBoomStick.source: item.cs SBoomStickImage::onFire, ItemData SBoomStick; baseProjData.cs SBoomStickBlast, BoomStickBlast; bindings.cs

Mfgl.summary: Tactical Nuke: a heavy launcher that fires a slow shell which detonates in a massive nuclear explosion; it needs a Containment Pack unless worn by a Juggernaught.
notes: Firing requires a Containment Pack (FgcPack) on the back or Juggernaught armor; without it, the launcher blows up in the user's face (radius 3, 15 damage, nuke type) and tells them 'Firing A Tactical Nuke With Out A Containment Pack Can Be Dangerous'. Using it prints the same requirement if not met.

Fires FgcShell. The shell is launched with a strong kickback; once it is at rest, 3 seconds later NuclearExplosion deals 1.5 nuke damage to everything in a 15x15x25 box and spawns the nuclear blast and cloud effect projectiles.
Buying it auto-buys a Containment Pack; selling the pack auto-sells the nuke. The Juggernaught's buying a PlasmaCannon, LasCannon or Hammer pack removes the nuke.

Team limit of 1 Mfgl; carried only by Heavy, DreadNaught and Juggernaught (only the DreadNaught can carry the Containment Pack, so a Heavy cannot fire it safely); unlike Shifter, station_list.cs lists Mfgl and MfglAmmo for remote inventory stations ($RemoteInvList 1). The admin help text says kills made with it do not earn credit.
Remove the pack and the nuke is unmounted (FgcPack::onUnmount).
Mfgl.source: item.cs MfglImage::onFire, Mfgl::onUse, buyItem; baseProjData.cs FgcShell, NuclearExplosion; admin.cs help text; station_list.cs

Booster1Pack.summary: Hidden tool item that represents the Mercenary's right shoulder booster.
notes: Not sold: it is given and mounted in tool slot 4 when a player takes Mercenary armor. Its image fires a short Booster puff (a RocketData projectile); the Mercenary's actual boost comes from the Beacon key.
Unlike Shifter, the mod has no Booster mine datablock or Booster mine functions (Mine.cs), only the RocketData puff, as in Shifter v1G.
Booster1PackImage::onDeactivate releases the backpack trigger when the image stops.

Booster2Pack.summary: Hidden tool item that represents the Mercenary's left shoulder booster.
notes: Given and mounted in tool slot 5 together with Booster1Pack when a player takes Mercenary armor; it only shows a Booster puff.

Booster mode (normal or advanced) is chosen with the remotebooster_norm / remotebooster_adv commands (bindings.cs); the Beacon key applies the boost. As with Booster1Pack, there is no Booster mine here.

Fixit.summary: Engineer Repair-Gun: a free built-in repair beam that does not need a Repair Pack, and here repairs far faster than in Shifter.
notes: Fires RepairBolt. Aimed at a teammate or a friendly object it repairs, and aimed at itself it auto-repairs. This mod's RepairBolt::onAcquire sets the repair rate to 2 in both cases (Shifter: 0.1 on a target and 0.05 on yourself).

If the target is undamaged it says so and stops. On completion RepairBolt::checkDone awards repair score (and takes it away for repairing enemy objects, or gives none if you were the last to damage the object); Guard Dog turrets were added to its score table. Unlike Shifter, onAcquire no longer records the starting damage in $PlayerRepairTar (only the Regeneration Gun still does), so the damage-based bonus in the score is zero unless the player has used the Regeneration Gun.
The Engineer gun has three switchable forms (repair, hack, disassembler) chosen from Engineer Options; switching swaps Fixit for Hackit or DisIt.
Carried by Engineer and, unlike Shifter, by the Heavy armor (which duel games use). Using it prints 'Using Engineer Repair-Gun'.
Fixit.source: item.cs ItemData Fixit; baseProjData.cs RepairBolt::onAcquire/onRelease/checkDone; bindings.cs remoteweapon_eng_*; itemmsgs.cs; ArmorData.cs

GravGun.summary: Grav Gun: a beam that pulls enemies toward you or pushes them away, depending on the selected setting.
notes: Tractor setting applies an impulse toward the shooter; repulse applies the opposite impulse; both do a little electricity damage.
Setting chosen from GravGun Options (shown only to Arbitor and Engineer).
Carried by Arbitor and Engineer. Using it prints 'Using Grav Gun'.
GravGun.source: item.cs ItemData GravGun; baseProjData.cs gravCharge, gravCharge::damageTarget; bindings.cs remoteweapon_gravgun_*; admin.cs; damage.cs

EnergyPack.summary: Energy Pack: a backpack that raises the wearer's energy supply.
notes: Its pack image has negative energy use (minEnergy -1, maxEnergy -3), so it adds energy instead of draining it, and mounting it switches it on automatically (EnergyPack::onMount triggers the backpack slot).
Unmounting it while a Laser Rifle is in the weapon slot unmounts the rifle. This is the same code as stock Tribes; only the validateShape lines were commented out.
Carried by every armor in the shop except Juggernaught (and not the Penis armor).

ShieldPack.summary: Shield Pack: converts the wearer's energy into a damage shield.
notes: Unlike stock, activating the pack sets a stronger shield (shieldStrength 0.022 instead of 0.012) and a shieldon flag.
The shield absorbs damage by draining energy; it absorbs less per energy against shrapnel and mortar damage, does not absorb electricity, and does not absorb Hyper Blaster damage at all.
Carried by every buyable armor except Juggernaught.

StealthShieldPack.summary: StealthShield Pack: a light shield that also hides the wearer from sensors, turrets and missile locks.
notes: Activating gives a weaker shield than the Shield Pack (0.012) and adds 20 points of sensor suppression; deactivating removes both.
The admin help text says it hides the user from turrets and locking missiles.
Carried by every buyable armor except Juggernaught.

RegenerationPack.summary: Regeneration Pack: a backpack that, on a second use, swaps the player's weapon for a Regeneration Gun that drains enemy targets to heal the wearer and powers up friendly equipment.
notes: First use mounts the pack; using it again mounts the Regen tool in the weapon slot (unmounting or dropping the pack removes it).

On an enemy-team player or object the beam deals flash damage (one twentieth of the target's max damage per check) and repairs the user by a fraction of that; it refuses to work on hackable objects ('RegenPack does not work on this').

On a friendly target it first builds up for $Shifter::HackTime (5) seconds, then: shields a teammate or flier (shieldStrength 0.025 for 240 s), switches on an unpowered inventory, ammo or command station for $Shifter::HackedTime seconds, upgrades the shielding of a friendly turret or pulse sensor, or adds 1000 energy to a deployable inventory/ammo station (up to a cap).
The overload warnings meant for repeatedly charging a deployable station sit after a return in the code and cannot run.
Carried only by Arbitor and Heavy. The in-game help text says it lets you heal yourself, which is only partly what the code does.
RegenerationPack.source: item.cs RegenerationPack::onUse/onUnmount/onDrop, ItemData Regen; baseProjData.cs DrainBolt::onAcquire/checkDone/onRelease; admin.cs help text

LightningPack.summary: Teleport Pack: an Arbitor-only backpack that teleports the wearer to a personal telepoint set by a thrown Telebeacon.
notes: Activating with no telepoint throws a Telebeacon mine; once it comes to rest it sets the player's telepoint. Activating again with a telepoint teleports the player there.
The code refuses if the telepoint is more than 300 m away (the message says 350 m). If a flag is carried there is a 50% chance it is dropped ('Teleport malfunction').

If the Telebeacon has been destroyed or disabled the telepoint is cleared and the player is told to set a new one. The 'Clear Telepoint' entry in Weapon Options lets an Arbitor reset it with an EMP blast at the old point.
The pack switches itself off after each use; the team limit on Telebeacons is 5 here (Shifter: 10).
LightningPack.source: item.cs LightningPackImage::onActivate/onDeactivate; itemfuncs.cs telebeacon; Mine.cs Telebeacon; admin.cs cleartelepoint; ArmorData.cs

FlightPack.summary: Flight Pack: an energy-boosting backpack for the light armors that keeps their jets running longer and recharges faster.
notes: Its pack image has negative energy use, like the Energy Pack, so it adds energy instead of draining it; mounting it switches it on automatically. The admin help text says it gives lighter armors a much greater energy supply and quicker regeneration.
Unmounting it unmounts a Laser Rifle in the weapon slot, so it can stand in for the Energy Pack that rifle needs.
Carried by Scout, Stim and Chemeleon, and (unlike Shifter) by the Heavy armor that the duel games use.
FlightPack.source: item.cs FlightPackImage, FlightPack::onUse/onMount/onUnmount; admin.cs help text; ArmorData.cs

SMRPack.summary: Rocket Launcher Pack: a shoulder-mounted auto-rocket launcher for the DreadNaught that fires one rocket each time it is activated.
notes: Activating it spends one Auto Rocket and fires a stinger: if the crosshair is on a player or flier within 950 m it fires a seeking StingerMissileTracker, shows 'Lock Aquired' and warns the target; otherwise it fires a plain stinger.
Its Chemeleon check is written '!= spyarmor || != spyfemale', which is always true, so Chemeleons can be locked.

With no ammo: 'You have no Ammo for the Auto Rocket Launcher'. Carried only by the DreadNaught. Its pack image fires on a much shorter cycle than in Shifter (reload 0.12, fire 0.05 against 0.9 and 1.0).

SMRPack2.summary: Rocket Launcher Pack variant given to the Juggernaught, with the same auto-rocket behavior as the DreadNaught's pack.
notes: Buying the Juggernaught armor gives this pack and mounts it. SMRPack2Image::onActivate runs the same lock-and-fire code as SMRPackImage (950 m lock on players and fliers, otherwise a plain stinger) and uses the same Auto Rocket ammo.
For a Juggernaught, buying this pack removes the Hammer packs and Hammer ammo, and buying a Hammer1Pack removes this pack: the heavy-weapon choices are mutually exclusive.
Same always-true Chemeleon check as SMRPack. Juggernaught only. Its pack image has shortened timing too (reload 0.12, fire 0.09 against 0.8 and 1.0).

BarragePack.summary: Anti-Aircraft Turret pack: a deployable missile turret that only fires at targets sitting in a vehicle.
notes: Deployed with deployable(): within 4 m, flat surface, clearance, frequency and no-inside checks, a flag-defense score bonus within 100 m of the flag, and a team limit of 3.

The BarrageTurret fires BarrageBolt, a fast seeking missile (missile damage type), range 325 m. Its verifyTarget returns true only for targets that have a mount object (vehicle riders and fliers) and raises the turret's shield strength while it has such a target.
Carried by DreadNaught, Engineer and Mercenary.
BarragePack.source: item.cs BarragePack::deployShape; turret.cs BarrageTurret; baseProjData.cs BarrageBolt

Laptop.summary: Command Laptop: a backpack that gives command access and hacking from the field.
notes: Turning it on sets the client's Laptop flag; Client::takeControl then lets the wearer take control of turrets and other remote items without standing in a Command Station, and Chemeleon and Engineer wearers can use it (with hack mode on) to re-program enemy turrets (turret.cs).
While on it checks every 3 seconds for enemy deployable sensor jammers within 200 m and prints the distance.
Carried by Engineer, Scout, Stim and Chemeleon.
Laptop.source: item.cs LaptopImage::onActivate/onDeactivate, LapTopImage::check; player.cs Client::takeControl; turret.cs; ArmorData.cs

SuicidePack.summary: Suicide DetPack: a Goliath backpack that is a drop-and-run bomb which blows up 20 seconds after it is dropped.
notes: Using it twice throws a Suicidebomb2 ('Det Pack will destruct in 20 seconds'), which explodes with a huge radius (100) and a nuclear blast effect. Team limit is $Shifter::DetPackLimit (25 in this mod's serverConfig.cs).
An Engineer who touches the armed bomb has a 50% chance to blow it up ('You cut the wrong wire') and otherwise disarms it.

If a Goliath carrying it kills themselves with the kill command, the pack goes off half a second later; an enemy laser, sniper or bullet hit to the torso sets it off on the wearer ('sniped the huge bomb').
SuicidePack.source: item.cs SuicidePack::deployShape; bombs.cs Suicidebomb2/Suicidebomb; remote.cs remoteKill; player.cs Player::onDamage; ArmorData.cs

AmmoPack.summary: Ammo Pack: a backpack that lets the wearer carry extra ammunition, with an expanded list of ammo types for Shifter's weapons.
notes: Unlike stock (7 ammo types), fillAmmoPack tops up 13 types (bullets, plasma, discs, grenade ammo, grenades, mines, mortar shells, beacons, boom shells, rockets, rail rounds, Vulcan rounds and dart ammo), but only for items the current armor can carry; with the pack mounted each type's $AmmoPackMax is added on top of the armor limit.
Dropping the pack hands whatever you hold above your normal limit to the pack, and picking it up gives it back; the drop and pickup code only handles the first 12 ammo types in the list.
Selling the pack re-runs checkMax so the extra ammo is sold off.
Carried by every buyable armor except Juggernaught.

PulseSensorPack.summary: Pulse Sensor pack: a deployable pulse sensor, a smaller version of the pulse sensors found in bases.
notes: Unlike stock, it deploys through Shifter's Item::deployShape as 'Remote Pulse Sensor', which also accepts deployed platforms as a surface; team limit 10.
Carried by every buyable armor except Juggernaught.
PulseSensorPack.source: item.cs PulseSensorPack::onDeploy; itemfuncs.cs Item::deployShape; admin.cs help text; ArmorData.cs

DeployableSensorJammerPack.summary: Sensor Jammer pack: a deployable jammer that hides you and your teammates from enemy sensors.
notes: Unlike stock, it deploys through deployable() (within 5 m, surface check, team limit 10) and can be placed on deployed platforms.
The Command Laptop detects enemy sensor jammers within 200 m.
Carried only by Engineer, Mercenary and Chemeleon.
DeployableSensorJammerPack.source: item.cs DeployableSensorJammerPack::deployShape; itemfuncs.cs deployable; item.cs LapTopImage::check; ArmorData.cs

CameraPack.summary: Backpack that places a Camera, a weaponless turret that can be dropped on terrain, buildings or deployable platforms. Shifter replaced stock Tribes' custom camera placement code with the shared deployable() helper.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, which had its own placement code that only allowed terrain and interiors within 3 m, Shifter lets you place it up to 5 m away on terrain, interiors, Deployable Platforms, Blast Walls and similar deployed surfaces. It is not required to be a flat surface; the camera is turned to face along the surface it hits (up, down or sideways).

The deployed CameraTurret has no projectile (it is only a viewing/spotting turret, range 50, narrow field of view) and very low health. Turret::onDamage lists CameraTurret as exempt from the server team-damage scale, so teammates damage it at full strength.
An Engineer can also create the same CameraTurret from a Beacon (Cloaking Camera beacon mode); that version is faded out (cloaked) and costs a Beacon instead of the pack.
The Disassymbler-Gun can dismantle a deployed camera and give the pack back.
Script bug: CameraTurret::onDestroyed decrements the CameraPack count correctly but then also decrements an 'EngBeacons' count using an undefined %player variable.
Viewing the camera feed (command station or laptop) is only described by the in-game help text; the camera code itself does not show how the feed is accessed.
CameraPack.source: item.cs CameraPack::onUse/onDeploy/deployShape; itemfuncs.cs deployable(); turret.cs CameraTurret; itemfuncs.cs EngCamera

ConPack.summary: Guard Dog: an Engineer backpack that deploys a remote turret firing slow, heavy, shockwave-sized rockets at anything in its range.
notes: Deployed with ConPack::deployShape: a 3 m line-of-sight reach, onto terrain, interiors or deployable platforms only, on a surface with a normal of at least 0.7 upward ('Can only deploy on flat surfaces'). It refuses if a Guard Dog is within the minimum-spacing box ('Frequency Overload - Too close to other remote turrets'), if the maximum-per-box count of Guard Dogs is reached ('Interference from other remote turrets in the area'), or if a player or item is in the way (checkDeployArea).

Team limit $TeamItemMax[ConPack] is 2 ('Deployable Item limit reached for Guard Dogs'). The count is raised on deployment and lowered again in DeployableConTurret::onDestroyed. The deployed turret is named 'RMT Guard Dog' with a running number.

DeployableConTurret (turret.cs, the 'watchdog turret') is a TurretData with the chainturret shape, range 190 and a 1.5 second reload; it fires the 'Watch' rocket, a slow missile-damage rocket with a very large blast radius (30) and strong knockback, and its deploy animation runs before it is switched active. Its shield strength is set to 0.010 on add. Its onPower function is empty, so it does not depend on base power.

Carried by the Engineer and the Heavy armor (ArmorData.cs); it is on the inventory-station and remote-station lists ($InvList and $RemoteInvList 1). RepairBolt::checkDone's score table has a 'Guard Dog' entry, so repairing one scores like a small turret.
Unlike the Shifter turret packs, ConPack does not go through deployable() and has no flag-defence score or no-offence-turret check.
ConPack.source: item.cs ConPack::onUse/onDeploy/deployShape, checkDeployArea, ItemData ConPack; turret.cs DeployableConTurret; baseProjData.cs Watch, RepairBolt::checkDone; station_list.cs; ArmorData.cs

TargetPack.summary: Backpack that deploys a remote Mortar Turret that lobs mortar shells at long range.
notes: The DeployableMortar turret uses the MortarShell projectile at range 150 with a 1.8 second reload. Its onFire override only echoes a debug line.
The in-game help text says it only fires when commanded; the scripts add no target filter or command logic for it (there is no verifyTarget), so how it chooses targets is not determined from scripts.

Deployed through the shared deployable() helper in itemfuncs.cs: flat surface, 'Frequency Overload' proximity limit, a headroom check (it refuses to deploy where the 14 units above the spot are blocked, 'space too enclosed'), clear spot, 4 m reach.
If the server option Shifter::TurretKill is on (it is on in this mod's serverConfig.cs), kills by this turret are credited to the player who deployed it.
Deploying it within the listed range of your own flag stand awards flag-defense score to the deployer. (within 25 of the flag).
Turret::onDamage lists DeployableMortar as exempt from the team-damage scale (teammates damage it at full strength).
Script bug: the deployed turret's map name is 'Mortar Turret # N <player>', but the Disassymbler-Gun looks for the name 'RMT Mortar Turret', so it can never be dismantled that way.
TargetPack.source: item.cs TargetPack::deployShape; turret.cs DeployableMortar; itemfuncs.cs deployable(); baseProjData.cs objectColapsable

RocketPack.summary: Backpack that deploys an RMT Rocket Turret, a seeking-missile turret that only engages high-heat targets and can shoot down enemy guided missiles.
notes: Fires TurretMissile seeking missiles with a 2.5 second reload at range 125. DeployableRocket::verifyTarget only allows targets whose heat factor is at least 0.5 (fliers report 1.0), so it ignores cold targets.

Once its deploy animation ends it runs DeployableRocket::missilecheck every 1.5 seconds: any enemy missile of the Missile Control Station family (Phoenix, Napalm, HaVoC, EMP, Toxin) within a 175-unit box is attacked by a MiniMissileTracker fired from the turret.
The same check also looks for an enemy DeployableSensorJammer in range; if one is found the turret takes 0.15 impact damage on each pass, so sensor jammers wear it down.
Deployed through the shared deployable() helper in itemfuncs.cs: flat surface, proximity limit, a 2.5 unit clearance, headroom check, 4 m reach.
If the server option Shifter::TurretKill is on (it is on in this mod's serverConfig.cs), kills by this turret are credited to the player who deployed it.
Deploying it within the listed range of your own flag stand awards flag-defense score to the deployer. (within 100 of the flag).
The Disassymbler-Gun recognizes 'RMT Rocket Turret'.

TreePack.summary: Backpack that plants a Mechanical Tree, a cosmetic tree that works as cover.
notes: Terrain only (not interiors): must be placed on flat terrain with a clear spot. It randomly picks tree model 1 (4 in 10) or tree model 2 (6 in 10); both are decorative StaticShapes with a health of 6.5 that do not show to sensors.
The proximity count for other trees is computed but its check is commented out, so trees can be packed together.
The in-game help text says it serves little purpose except for cover. The Disassymbler-Gun cannot dismantle it (no entry for it).

PlantPack.summary: Backpack that plants a Healing Plant, a cactus that repairs any damaged player who touches it.
notes: While a damaged player touches DeployableCactus2, GameBase::repairDamage heals them by 0.3 and plays the force-field sound. There is no team check, so enemies are healed too. Rocket-shaped missiles that touch it are destroyed.

On deployment it randomly picks DeployableCactus2 (6 in 10) or DeployableCactus1 (4 in 10). Script bug: no DeployableCactus1 datablock is defined anywhere in the scripts, so about 4 in 10 deployments ask for a missing object while still reporting 'Healing Plant Deployed' and using up the pack.
Placed on flat terrain or buildings, 3 m reach, clear spot needed. Very low health (0.5). The Disassymbler-Gun can pick it up ('Healing Plant').

TeleportPack.summary: Backpack that places a Teleport Pad; a team that deploys two pads can step between them.
notes: Deployed on flat ground 5 m away; it is raised 1 unit and gets an electrical beam effect. Pad count uses the team 'DeployableTeleport' limit.
Walking onto a pad sends you to the first other pad of your team, then both pads are disabled for 5 seconds ('Teleport Pad is recharging'). With no second pad you get 'No other pad to teleport to'.

Heavy and DreadNaught armor (harmor, darmor) cannot teleport. Enemies get 'Wrong Team' unless they wear Chameleon armor, which can phase through and is sent to an enemy pad ('Transporting To Enemy Telepad').
Destroying one pad deals heavy damage (20) to one other pad of the same team, so the pair dies together.
Rocket-shaped missiles touching a pad are destroyed.

MechPack.summary: Backpack that deploys an armed Scout flier (the 'Interceptor') at the spot you aim at.
notes: MechPack::deployShape spawns a standard Scout flier on the player's team with an InterceptorModule already loaded (module 9, 150 shots). The in-game help text says it is weaponless, but the script preloads the Interceptor gun module.
Its fire button launches two InterceptorAmmo bullets at a time, 0.1 seconds apart, using one of the 150 shots each time.
Needs a flat spot within 10 m that passes the clear-area check; counted by the 'MechPack' team limit.
Only light-class armors (Assassin, Scout, Chameleon, Stim) can pilot Shifter fliers; see the Vehicle::onCollision code.

DetPack.summary: Backpack that deploys an HAPC flier (heavy personnel carrier), named 'Stealth HPC' in the shop.
notes: DetPack::deployShape places a regular HAPC flier on the player's team with the map name 'HPC Pack'. It must be set on terrain or an interior, on flat ground, within 3 m.
It is counted against the shared HAPC vehicle team limit ('HAPCVehicle'), not a pack-specific limit.
The vehicle comes with no module loaded. HAPCs accept the Stealth, GodHammer and Bomber modules (see those items). The name suggests stealth, but the pack itself adds no cloaking.
The item named 'Suicide DetPack' in item.cs and the 'DetPack Module' for Scout fliers are different things.

RepairKit.summary: A carried medical kit that heals the user and cures poison, with a different amount of healing per armor.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes (a flat 0.2 repair for everyone), the heal depends on the armor: Juggernaught 0.5; Engineer and DreadNaught 0.3; Chameleon, Mercenary, Arbitor, Heavy and Goliath 0.2; Scout, Assassin and any other armor 0.1.
It also cures poison ($poisonTime reset to 0, 'Poison cured').
Scout armors (including the Stim variant) also lower their overdose counter by 20 to 44 points if it is above 15.
Juggernaught additionally reduces its heat-up counter by 20 when above 50.
The Engineer's Beacon in 'MediKit' mode throws a RepairKit item to teammates.

MineAmmo.summary: The mine item. Instead of stock Tribes' single antipersonnel mine, each armor class throws a different kind of mine.
notes: Assassin: a flag-shaped decoy mine ('Hologram' mine) that explodes on enemy contact.
Chameleon: a cloaking Subspace mine (fades out).
Arbitor: a ShockWave mine that fades out after 8 seconds, detonates 0.2 seconds after an enemy touches it.
Scout, Mercenary, Heavy and Goliath: the standard Antipersonel mine.

Engineer: depends on the mine mode set in the weapon options: Proximity Detector (a radar mine that only announces 'Incoming Enemies' to the team, at most once per 10 seconds, within about 20 units), Cloaking mine, Point Defense Laser mine (costs 15 energy and is placed on the surface you look at), Standard mine, or Replicator mine (when destroyed it spawns two copies up to a fixed generation).

DreadNaught: by default a Point Defense Laser mine (costs 10 energy, explodes after Shifter::LaserMineLive seconds, which this mod's serverConfig.cs sets to 7); can be switched to standard mines with the DMine option.
Juggernaught, P-armor and the temporary Stim Scout armor have no matching branch, so they throw no usable mine.
All mines are thrown from the player, set to the thrower's team and do not trigger on teammates. They only work after the match starts.

Grenade.summary: The grenade item. Instead of stock Tribes' single hand grenade, the thrown grenade depends on armor class.
notes: Mercenary: the standard fragmentation Handgrenade (2 second fuse).
Scout (and Stim): a Firebomb with an electric blast radius of 35 and strong knockback.
Assassin: a 'HoloMine', a mine that looks like an armor/repair pack, detonates when an enemy touches it, and blows itself up after 120 seconds.
Engineer: an EMP grenade (flash damage, radius 25).
Chameleon: a Plastique charge (the sticky 'Nukebomb') that explodes after the delay the player chose in the Plastique options (2, 5, 10 or 15 seconds).
Arbitor: a Tranquilizer grenade that does energy damage.
Goliath: a Concussion grenade (plasma damage, radius 15).

DreadNaught: a Mortar grenade that explodes after 5 seconds or 0.1 seconds after a player touches it. Heavy: a Plastique-type 'Nukebomb' with no fuse scheduled in the grenade code, so it only goes off if damaged.
Juggernaught and the P-armor have no matching branch. Thrown grenades are team-tagged. Any Engineer who touches a Plastique has a 70 percent chance to disarm it (and 30 percent to set it off).
Throw speed is 15 times the player's throw strength, versus 9 times in stock Tribes.
Note: the comment block at the top of grenade.cs lists a different assignment (Scout concussion, Goliath firebomb); the item.cs code is what applies.

Beacon.summary: The Beacon item has been turned into a multi-purpose armor ability. Instead of stock Tribes' simple target beacon, each armor class gets a different action.
notes: Assassin: tosses a Detbomb mine (negative throw strength) with a 5 second fuse, or 0.1 seconds after any player touches it.

Engineer: depends on the Engineer Beacon option: standard Target Beacon, a cloaked Camera, or a MediKit (throws a RepairKit to teammates). The 'Anti-Missile Screen' option can be selected in the menu but Beacon::onUse has no branch for it. Limited by the 'EngBeacons' team limit (10).
Scout (and Stim): a Stim Pack. Swaps to Stim armor for about 10 seconds and heals 0.035 every 2 seconds, with a growing overdose chance that can kill the player; at the end the armor reverts.
Chameleon: deploys a Satchel Charge (a DeployableSatchel turret, up to 15 per team) on the surface you aim at; it applies mine-type radius damage when triggered (onFire/onControl).
Juggernaught: begins charging the LasCannon or HeavyPlasmaCannon (10 or 8 second charge); fails with a message if neither is carried.
Mercenary: fires the Speed Booster, a mass-scaled impulse (normal mode forward and up; advanced mode in the aim direction) with a cooldown. The Booster is consumed per use.
Arbitor: starts a 20-second cloak (fade-out plus sensor suppression); the Beacon is consumed.
Goliath: throws a Concussion2 grenade (plasma damage, radius 35, 5 second fuse, 0.15 second throw delay).

DreadNaught and Heavy: activate an emergency force shield (shield strength 0.006) that lasts 20 seconds. The shield-check function only keeps the timer going for DreadNaught/Juggernaught armor, so the Heavy's shield ends at its next 2 second check.
Script observation: SniperJammer and ScoutSensor exist in itemfuncs.cs but nothing calls them.

AirAmmoPad.summary: Backpack that drops a Spy Station base pad with an ammo station on it, for air vehicles to resupply.
notes: Placed at the player's own position (not the line of sight). It needs a 15x15x10 clear area and must be more than 10 units from your own flag stand ('You are too close to your flag').
It creates two objects: an AirAmmoBasePad platform (6x6 thin elevator, health 5) and a DeployableAmmoStation on it, both on the player's team.
Script bug: the function never increments the AirAmmoPad team count, so the team limit of 4 is never reached.

airbase.summary: Backpack that builds a complete floating Air Base 180 units above the player: six platforms, generator, command station, inventory station, vehicle pad and station, and a pulse sensor.
notes: airbase::deployshape builds twelve team-owned pieces relative to the player: six LargeAirBasePlatform slabs, a Portable Generator, a Command Station, an Inventory Station, a Vehicle Pad with a Vehicle Station, and a Pulse Sensor, all in a per-player set. Unlike Shifter, the base is built at +180.5 height instead of +50.5, and there are two more slabs (Platform5 and Platform6).
It needs a 45x45x25 clear volume at the build position, and is carried by the Engineer.
Script bug: the two new slabs are added to the sets but never marked as part of the base (the lines meant for them look up %plat11 and %plat12, which are never assigned).
Script bug: the code reads the airbase team count to name the pieces but never compares it with the limit of 3, so the limit is not enforced here, and nothing decrements the count.

Leaving the mission area while carrying this pack blows the carrier up (Player::leaveMissionArea); duelmod.cs replaces that function with an empty one. It is also on the remote inventory list here ($RemoteInvList[Airbase] is 1; Shifter 0).
airbase.source: item.cs airbase::deployshape; player.cs Player::leaveMissionArea; station_list.cs; ArmorData.cs

LaunchPack.summary: Backpack that places a Launch Pad that flings anything that touches it forward and up.
notes: Any object that collides with the DeployableLaunch pad (player or otherwise, friend or foe, there is no team check) gets an impulse of 200 forward and 600 up relative to the object's own rotation, plus a mortar sound and a 'SPROING!' message.
Placed on flat terrain or interiors, 3 m reach, health 1.5, invisible to sensors. Rocket-shaped missiles touching it are destroyed.
The Disassymbler-Gun can pick it up ('Launchboard').

AccelPPack.summary: Backpack that places an Accelerator Pad, which boosts teammates who jump or jet off it.
notes: Only teammates are affected. When a teammate stands on top of the pad, a message tells them to face the desired direction and then jump or jet; you can walk off to avoid being launched.

A 0.05 second check detects the player rising above the pad, then applies an impulse in their facing direction scaled by their armor mass: full strength (50 forward, 50 up per unit of mass) for Scout, Chameleon, Assassin and Stim, reduced for Mercenary, Goliath, Engineer and Arbitor (40 and 35), and strongly reduced (15 and 15) for DreadNaught, Juggernaught and P-armor. The base Heavy armor appears in none of these lists, so it gets the full default.
The pad is health 3.3 and when placed the deployer is moved on top of it. Rocket-shaped missiles touching it are destroyed.
Per-team limit comes from AccelPPack; the count is raised in onDeploy.

Regen.summary: The Regeneration Gun, a drain beam mounted from the Regeneration Pack that damages powered enemy equipment while healing the user, and can power up friendly equipment.
notes: It is not sold or listed in the inventory; RegenerationPack::onUse mounts it into the weapon slot on a second use.
Used on an enemy structure from the checkHackable list, it applies flash damage each tick equal to one twentieth of the target's max damage and repairs the user by 1/25 of that amount.

Used on friendly equipment for the hack time, it can: give a teammate a 0.025 shield for 240 seconds, shield a flier, power an inventory/ammo/command station for Shifter::HackedTime seconds, upgrade shielding on base turrets and pulse sensors to 0.03, or add 1000 energy to deployable stations.
checkDone first rejects any shape not on checkHackable's list ('RegenPack does not work on this'), which appears to make the player and flier branches unreachable.

Plastique.summary: A throwable Plastique charge item that is not stocked in any inventory.
notes: Plastique::onUse throws the sticky 'Nukebomb' charge at a gentle throw speed of 4 times throw strength, on the thrower's team, after the match has started.

The message promises it will explode in a number of seconds but the item code never schedules the detonation (unlike the Chameleon's Grenade, which does) and reads the delay from the player, not the client, so it is likely blank. The charge only goes off if damaged. An Engineer who touches an enemy charge has a 70 percent chance of disarming it and a 30 percent chance of setting it off.

$InvList[Plastique] is 0, $RemoteInvList[Plastique] is 3 here (Shifter 0), and no armor lists it in $ItemMax, so players cannot buy or carry it; the Chameleon's Plastique comes through the Grenade key instead.

RepairPatch.summary: The floor/pickup repair patch, now healing by armor class and curing poison.
notes: Unlike stock Tribes, where touching a patch repairs a flat 0.125 and using one repairs 0.1, Shifter's onCollision (touch) now runs the same armor-based repair as RepairPatch::onUse: Engineer and DreadNaught 0.3; Chameleon, Mercenary, Arbitor, Heavy, Goliath 0.2; Scout, Assassin and others 0.1.
It also cures poison and gives scout armors an overdose reduction, like the Repair Kit.
Touch healing only happens if the player is damaged, after which the patch plays its pickup sound and respawns.

Unlike the Repair Kit, there is no special case for the Juggernaught (it gets the default 0.1), and RepairPatch::onUse no longer calls Player::decItemCount, so using a carried patch would not use it up.

EmplacementPack.summary: Backpack that builds a Defense Emplacement: a raised platform with two inventory stations and a ring of force fields, built around the player.
notes: Deploys on flat terrain only within 6 m, with a clear area. It spawns three LargeEmplacementPlatform slabs (Shifter: two), two Inventory Stations (Shifter: one), a Portable Generator, and ten static force-field panels (six 4x8 and four 3x4; Shifter: five). All pieces are team-owned and flagged as part of the base. No opening script is defined for the panels, so they act as solid translucent walls.
The generator is placed 615 units below the player instead of 15, so it sits far underground.
Script bug: the team limit check is commented out, so the limit of 2 is not enforced.

It also provides the rotVector() helper used by the Disc Launcher and other scripts. It is on the remote inventory list here ($RemoteInvList[EmplacementPack] is 1; Shifter 0) and is carried by the Engineer.
Leaving the mission area while carrying this pack blows the carrier up (duelmod.cs replaces that function with an empty one). It is flagged in $CanAlwaysTeamDestroy, so teammates can destroy it.

LasCannon.summary: A Juggernaught-only heavy weapon charged with Beacons that unleashes a barrage of laser bolts, but overloads and kills the user if held too long.
notes: Press the Beacon key to start charging (consumes a Beacon): the weapon mounts and charges one level per second for 10 seconds, then sets full charge (15).

Firing releases a burst whose size depends on the charge: LasCannonBolts at any charge, extra bolts and LasCannonShock at above 3, GatlingLaser at above 5 and above 7, more at above 9, and a LasCannonBolt2 at full charge. Firing without a charge only says it uses Beacons.
At full charge the user has 15 seconds to fire; otherwise they explode (HavocBlast).
Only Juggernaught can carry it ($ItemMax). Buying it clears the Plasma Cannon and God Hammer cannons from the player's inventory.

PlasmaCannon.summary: A Juggernaught-only heavy plasma weapon charged with Beacons that fires a heavy plasma barrage and explodes the user if left overloaded.
notes: Press the Beacon key to start an 8 second charge (consumes a Beacon); the charge level rises one per second then sets full charge (15).

Firing releases PlasmaCannonBolt and PlasmaCannonBolt2 bolts and PlasmaCannonShock shells in a pattern that grows with charge. At full charge it also launches two PlasmaCannonShock2 shells that scatter frag debris when they are removed.
At full charge the user has 15 seconds to fire; otherwise they explode (HavocBlast plus extra plasma damage).
Firing without a charge only says it uses Beacons.

Hammer1Pack.summary: The right-hand God Hammer Cannon, one of a Juggernaught's twin shoulder cannons that fire explosive rockets.
notes: Buying Hammer1Pack automatically grants Hammer2Pack and mounts the two into shoulder slots 4 and 5. Using the weapon key via the backpack path fires both cannons together (a GodHammer rocket, explosion damage, radius 15) if the player has any HammerAmmo.

Each volley adds 5 heat: above 50 percent the cannon shows an overheating warning, above 65 it burns the user lightly, above 80 it does steady plasma damage, and over 99 it detonates the user with frag fragments. Heat drains gradually (4 per cooling tick).
Only Juggernaught can carry it. Buying it removes the Las and Plasma cannons.
Hammer1Pack.source: item.cs Hammer1Pack, remoteUseItem, GodHammer::HeatUp/HeatCheck/CoolDown; baseProjData.cs GodHammer

Hammer2Pack.summary: The left-hand God Hammer Cannon, the hidden second half of the Juggernaught's paired shoulder cannons.
notes: Hidden from the inventory (showInventory false). It is added with Hammer1Pack and fired together with it; it shares the same GodHammer projectile and HammerAmmo.
Mounted in slot 5 beside Hammer1Pack's slot 4. Selling Hammer1Pack removes it.
